definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese low table with an electric heater underneath and a blanket that drapes over the sides to trap heat, used for warming the lower body during cold weather.

examples.english: I don't want to get out of the kotatsu.
You'll catch a cold if you fall asleep in the kotatsu.

notes:
The {炬燵|こたつ} is a quintessential Japanese winter comfort item. It consists of a low wooden table frame covered with a ⟦{布団|ふとん}→布団：01720_futon⟧ or heavy blanket, with a heat source underneath. Modern kotatsu typically use electric heaters.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {炬燵|こたつ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{入|はい}る→入る：00494_hairu⟧ (to get into the kotatsu)
- {炬燵|こたつ}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{出|で}る→出る：00513_deru⟧ (to get out of the kotatsu)
- {炬燵|こたつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{出|だ}す→出す：01087_dasu⟧ (to set up the kotatsu)
- {炬燵|こたつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦しまう→しまう：03064_shimau⟧ (to put away the kotatsu)

CULTURAL NOTE:
- Traditionally associated with eating ⟦みかん→みかん：01036_mikan⟧ (mandarin oranges) while staying warm in winter.
- The combination of {炬燵|こたつ}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦みかん→みかん：01036_mikan⟧ is a stereotypical image of Japanese winter comfort.
- Sleeping in the {炬燵|こたつ} is considered unhealthy as only the lower body stays warm.
